name: Geo
classification_notes: An all-caps experimental sans-serif display typeface defined by its technical concept rather than conventional typographic construction. The emphasis on extreme anchor-point density produces letterforms of unusual structural complexity rather than a traditional classification character.
summary: An experimental all-caps display font built around pushing font files to their anchor-point capacity.
description: Geo is an all-caps experimental display typeface from Lena Weber's x*y Monomodular foundry. The concept centres on maximising the number of anchor points a font file can hold, producing letterforms of unusual structural complexity. The character set covers uppercase, numerals and basic punctuation only – there is no lowercase.
foundry_blurb: GEO is described as an experimental font pushing the limits of how many anchor points a font file can store. The guiding idea, as the foundry puts it: nothing is set in stone.

name: Bezier
classification_notes: A curvy headline display typeface with a modular grid-based construction. Named for Bézier curve logic, the letterforms are defined by smooth rounded forms. A fixed-width companion (Bezier Mono) extends the family, but the primary face is display-oriented.
summary: A curvy display typeface built on Bézier curve logic, with a fixed-width companion variant.
description: Bezier is a headline display typeface with pronounced curves throughout, constructed on a 600×600-unit modular grid. The letterforms take their logic from Bézier curves, producing smooth rounded forms that sit apart from conventional display faces. A Bezier Mono companion extends the design into fixed-width territory, with coverage across full Latin and Latin Extended character sets.
foundry_blurb: Bezier is a curvy typeface designed on a modular grid, covering the full Latin character range. A Bezier Mono companion brings the same rounded character to a fixed-width format.

name: Abraxas
classification_notes: A variable typeface that spans from legible letterforms to abstract geometric squares as the variable axes shift. Sits at the boundary between typography and generative art; practical typesetting use is very limited.
summary: A variable hybrid font where letterforms progressively dissolve into unreadable geometric squares.
description: Abraxas is a variable font from Lena Weber's x*y Monomodular foundry in which letterforms transition into abstract squares as the variable axes are pushed. Both uppercase and lowercase Latin are covered, built on a 600×600-unit modular grid with adjustable stretch and curve parameters. At readable settings it functions as a display face; at extremes it becomes a pattern generator.
foundry_blurb: Abraxas is described as a variable hybrid font where the shapes transform into unreadable squares. The adjustable parameters for stretch and curves make it operate simultaneously as a typeface and a system for generating geometric patterns.
